 Order

This writ petition is filed for following reliefs:
a) Issue a Writ of Certiorari quashing the General Award bearing No.KIADB:LAQ No.588/2023-24 dated 19.05.2023 passed by Respondent No.3 in respect of land bearing Survey no.28/6 measuring 0.08 guntas situated at Obalapura village,
Thyamagoundlu Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bangaluru Rural District, as per Annexure-C;
b) Issue any suitable order, direction or writ in nature of Mandamus directing the Respondents herein to consider the case of Petitioner as per Section 29(2) of the KIAD Act etc.

2. Sri Mahesh D., learned counsel for petitioner submitted that, petitioner was absolute owner of land bearing Survey no.28/6, measuring 0.08 guntas of land, situated at Obalapura village,
Thyamagoundlu Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District.

It was further submitted that respondent - authority had initiated acquisition proceedings in NC: 2023:KHC:40686 respect of aforesaid land for forming industrial area, when petitioner filed objections seeking for dropping of his lands from acquisition.
But, respondent no.3 recommended for acquisition of petitioner's land and issued notifications under Section 28(3) of KIAD Act, 1966.

It was submitted that without affording opportunity to petitioner, respondent no.3 passed award under Section 29(3) of KIAD Act,

2 which was under challenge.

sentences.text: It was contended that under consent award, compensation was considerably higher than under General Award.

It was submitted that under similar circumstances,
this Court allowed several writ petitions, including W.P.no.22091/2022 disposed of on 30.11.2022 holding such denial as illegal, quashed General Award and directed respondents to consider petitioner's representation for passing consent award.
Hence sought for passing similar order.

3. Sri Manjunath V Rayappa, learned AGA for respondent no.1 and Sri P.V. Chandrashekar, learned counsel for respondent nos.2 and 3 submitted that in view of earlier decisions, respondent no.3 would consider representation, in accordance with law and sought for disposal of writ petition.
Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition record.

5. From above, it is seen that in W.P.no.22091/2022 contention of petitioner therein about failure to provide opportunity to accept compensation under consent award which was higher than under General award was held illegal, this Court set aside General Award and directed respondents to consider petitioner's representation for passing consent award.
Said decision would squarely apply in this case.

6. Accordingly, Writ petition is disposed of, impugned General Award bearing No.KIADB:LAQ no.588/2023-24 dated 19.05.2023 at Annexure-'C' passed by respondent no.3 in respect of land bearing Survey no.28/6, measuring 0.08 guntas situated at Obalapura village, Thyamagoundlu Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bangaluru Rural District,
is hereby quashed insofar as it relates to petitioner, is hereby set aside.
Respondent no.3 shall consider petitioner's representation and pass appropriate orders thereon within a period of eight weeks.

NC: 2023:KHC:40686 Needles to observe that direction issued to consider representation shall not be construed as a positive direction to grant relief sought in representation, but only as a direction to consider representation on its own merit in accordance with law.
Sd/-
